w1.title: Worked Example 1: Autotrophic Nutrition & Stages of Photosynthesis
w1.question: List the three core events that occur during photosynthesis in a leaf.

steps.text: Step 1: Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll in chloroplasts.
Step 2: Conversion of light energy into chemical energy and splitting of water (H₂O) into hydrogen and oxygen.
Step 3: Reduction of carbon dioxide (CO₂) to carbohydrates (glucose).

check.q: From which molecule does the oxygen gas released during photosynthesis come?

opts.m: Photolysis splits water molecules to release O₂.
Oxygen gas comes from water absorbed by roots.

w2.title: Worked Example 2: Stomata, Guard Cells & Eco Seva Mulching
w2.question: How does mulching around native saplings conserve soil water in summer?

steps.text: Direct sun heats bare topsoil and accelerates evaporation.
A dry-leaf mulch layer shades the root zone and cools the soil.
Reduced evaporation keeps water available for guard cells and root uptake.

check.q: What causes stomatal pores to open during the day?

opts.t: Water flows into guard cells, making them turgid
Guard cells lose all water and shrink
opts.m: Shrinking (flaccid) guard cells close the stomatal pore.
Turgor pressure inside guard cells opens the pore.

w3.title: Worked Example 3: Aerobic vs Anaerobic Cellular Respiration
w3.question: Why do muscle cramps occur during sudden heavy exercise?

steps.text: During sprint exercise, oxygen supply to muscle cells falls short.
Pyruvate is converted anaerobically into 3-carbon lactic acid.
Accumulation of lactic acid in muscle tissue causes temporary cramps.

check.q: Where does the complete aerobic breakdown of pyruvate take place?

opts.m: Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm; aerobic oxidation occurs in mitochondria.
Mitochondria are the powerhouses of aerobic ATP synthesis.

steps.title: Autotrophic Nutrition & Stages of Photosynthesis
steps.body: Green plants synthesize glucose using sunlight, chlorophyll, carbon dioxide, and water: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

steps.title: Stomata, Guard Cells & Eco Seva Mulching
steps.body: Tiny pores called stomata on leaf surfaces control gas exchange and transpiration. Guard cells swell with water to open the pore and shrink to close it.

steps.title: Aerobic vs Anaerobic Cellular Respiration
steps.body: Glucose (6-carbon) breaks down into pyruvate (3-carbon) in the cytoplasm. With oxygen in mitochondria, pyruvate yields CO₂, H₂O, and 38 ATP.
